title: Communication failure inquiry: why precision does not transfer from code to process
description:
Open line of inquiry, opened 2026-09-20 from a session where the owner had to raise agent communication quality three times.

Document: docs/communication-inquiry.md

Question: why does an agent that cites file and line when writing about code stop citing when writing about its own work, its own reasoning, or the user's complaint?

Standing hypothesis: fluency is cheap for the agent to produce and expensive for the reader to audit, which selects for errors that survive casual reading. Predicts clustering where nothing external can check the claim, and where the agent has no result to report. Both held in the observed session. Four data points, one session, agent-selected - a hypothesis, not a finding.

Eleven patterns recorded with quotes, one of them withdrawn in place as a false positive (and itself an instance of pattern 10, verification suppressed by agreement).

Open: whether the asymmetry is the cause or one of several; why written prohibitions had low durability (the same class recurred in the same session after the rules were written); whether the failure is detectable by the agent at generation time at all.

Next: collect instances from further sessions before strengthening any claim. Do not generalise from the single session already recorded.
notes:
2026-09-20: pattern 11 added, manufactured accountability. Corrected on an error, the agent supplied a preventable cause ('I should have checked the transcript ordering') for a fact not observable to it - messages compose concurrently, so transcript order does not establish authorship order. The first fabrication ran toward the user; so did its remedy. Added a section, 'What an agent can and cannot observe here'.
2026-09-23 owner explicitly requires dialogic responses including handoff. Recorded Metabrain incident and revised result/request-only framing; mixed process and product requests must receive both substantive conversation and authorized work. Causal hypothesis remains unproven.
